Hi Danielle — thanks for the clear list. I've attached an annotated SLA snippet (SLA_Draft_v2.pdf) and a quick diagram showing queue-shaping behavior. Key points up front:

- Measurement: tail-latency is measured per-reservation over rolling 30-day windows at the request-token level; we report 50/95/99/99.9 percentiles. Breaches for credits are triggered when 99.9th > agreed threshold during the measurement window.
- Nightly batch carveout: we support an agreed nightly window (customer-defined, e.g., 02:00–05:00 UTC) where the reservation has a relaxed throughput floor but is covered by a scheduled maintenance/eviction policy. If SprintGrid elects a nightly batch carveout, headroom credits are calculated pro rata for the window and shown as a separate line item.
- Observability: we will grant SprintGrid access to a read-only dashboard with token-level traces, per-model queue depth, and preemption events. Dashboards include alert rules that map to the SLA breach logic.

I've bolded the minimal legal language in the attached PDF to make redlines easier — see section 2.3 (measurement) and 4.1 (carveouts & credits).

Next steps: Marcus from Engineering will add a short technical note on how our queue-shaper enforces fairness and headroom. If Procurement wants, we can also produce a sample 30-day report.

Thanks,

Hey team — quick engineering note to clarify how queue-shaping works for a reserved pool, and the kinds of metrics you'll see in the dashboard. I'll keep it high-level for Legal/SRE: 

- Per-tenant inflight slots: a reservation is allocated a numeric budget of concurrent inflight token slots (example: 25k inflight tokens). Requests consume slots proportional to input+output token count; long-running streaming calls hold slots until the stream closes.
- Fairness & preemption: when the pool approaches capacity, the queue-shaper enforces soft limits by delaying low-priority requests (micro-backs-off) and preempting best-effort workloads first. Reserved requests for SprintGrid are pinned to the reserved pool and only preempted for emergency maintenance or explicit scheduled carveouts.
- Measurement signals exposed: per-request latency, queue-depth histogram (1s buckets), preemption events (with reason codes), GPU utilization per-slab, and per-model kv-cache hit rate. We publish analytic exports (CSV) for your billing/admin account.
- Example thresholds (proposal): throughput floor = 80% of baseline sustained throughput over 30-day window; tail-latency SLO 99.9 < 220ms for our Llama-optimized SKU; headroom credit if sustained drop below floor for >= 60 minutes within the measurement window.

I'll attach the queue diagram Marcus referenced in the SLA. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with SprintGrid SREs to walk through traces.

—Marcus

Hi Procurement — thanks for the precise asks. Below are short redline-ready paragraphs you can paste into the PO. If Contracts prefers different language we can adapt.

1) Measurement window
Redwood measures SLA metrics on a calendar-month basis for credit calculations. Rolling-window monitoring remains available in the dashboard for operational diagnostics.

2) Credits formula (example)
If the reservation sustained throughput is below the agreed throughput floor for more than 60 cumulative minutes in the calendar month, Redwood will apply a credit equal to (minutes_below_floor / total_minutes_in_month) * monthly_reservation_fee. For tail-latency breaches (99.9th percentile exceeding threshold), credits are computed as a separate line: (exceedance_count / total_sampling_periods) * penalty_coefficient. Example: a 5% sustained throughput shortfall over 2 hours in November on a $100k monthly reservation results in credit = (120 / 43200) * 100000 = $277.78.

3) Observability access
SprintGrid will receive SSO access to the read-only dashboard via SAML2.0; SCIM provisioning is supported for user/role sync. No VPN or VPC peering is required for dashboard access. For customers requesting cross-account logs export, we support an optional push to an S3/GCS bucket under SprintGrid's account (customer-managed keys).

Eric from CloudOps is copied; he requested to confirm the shape of the exported traces for his integration.

I'll also create a Jira under SGD-110 with the monitoring playbook deliverable and attach the sample 30-day report.
